cards.explanation: The answer is True. God says to Ezekiel, "Then declare to them their abominations." Ezekiel is the one who has to speak it out loud. I think that's a heavy job, friends, and it shows how seriously God takes what comes next.

The answer is idols. God says, "They have committed adultery with their idols." He uses the picture of a faithful marriage and says they gave themselves to something else. Idols are the other love in this picture, friends.

The answer is False. The sisters didn't stay away. The text says that on the very day, "…they entered My sanctuary to profane it." God says it happened "…inside My house." I think this is one of the hardest lines in the whole passage, friends.

The answer is that they bathe and paint their eyes. God says, "…you bathed for them, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry." The sisters get ready for the men who came from afar, the way you'd get ready for company, friends. They sent messengers for those men, and then they got dressed up for them.

The answer is His incense and His oil. God says the sisters sat on a couch with a table spread before it, "…on which you had set My incense and My oil…" Notice the word "My" in there, bakers. These were God's things, and they ended up on the wrong table.

The answer is that she's been unfaithful a long time. "…grown old in adulteries…" tells you the unfaithfulness isn't new, friends. It's been going on for a long time. In this picture, she didn't wander off yesterday.

The answer is righteous. God says, "But righteous men will sentence them to the punishment of those who commit adultery and bloodshed…" The ones who sentence them are described as righteous, bakers. The sisters are charged with adultery and with blood on their hands.

The answer is burn down. The mob will "…and burn down their houses." It's a heavy verse, friends. The same verse says they will stone the sisters, cut them down with swords and kill their sons and daughters. I think this is one of the places in the passage where it's right to go quiet for a second.

The answer is True. God says, "So I will put an end to indecency in the land…" He isn't leaving it, friends. He says what He will do. The same verse says all the women will be admonished not to imitate the sisters' behavior.

The answer is that He is the Lord GOD. God ends with, "Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD." The whole passage closes on who He is, friends. The sisters will bear the consequences of their sins of idolatry, and then they will know Him.
